text.p: The December 18 Tourism Council has been cancelled following continued disagreement on funding for the Commission's proposal on a first multiannual programme to assist European tourism in 1997 to 2000.
An EU source said some member states, in particular Germany, were reluctant to agree to funds for the Philoxenia (Hospitality) programme.
It is the third time this year that a Tourism Council has been postponed or cancelled.
Last April Tourism Commissioner Christos Papoutsis launched the tourism programme, hailing it as a boon to the quality and competitiveness of the European tourism industry.
Planned measures included improving information about tourism and removing barriers to the industry's development.
The programme has a planned budget of 25 million Ecus for 1997-2000.

Earlier this month, the European Federation of Conference Towns expressed disappointment over the failure to agree on the programme for what it said was Europe's biggest industry with great potential for GDP and job creation.

"We hope Philoxenia can be rescued from the neglect that threatens it, the victim of certain members who feel that tourism should remain a non-activity, while Europe continues to lose congress and other tourism business year by year to other destinations," it said in a statement.
